decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "The library has no thread-spawning code of its own." and "`mbedtls_threading_key_slot_mutex` ... `library/threading.c:182-190`... The default lock implementation is pthread: `mbedtls_mutex_lock` is a function pointer initialised to `threading_mutex_lock_pthread` (`threading.c:103`)." | WHY: The answer says the library spawns no threads (all spawn sites are in programs/) and that library/threading.c supplies the mutex abstraction (mutex init, lock function pointers, pthread default) for threaded callers. || QUOTE: "The index finds 4 spawn sites, all in `programs/`, none in `library/`" and "The library has no thread-spawning code of its own." plus "`mbedtls_mutex_lock` is a function pointer initialised to `threading_mutex_lock_pthread` (`threading.c:103`)" and "Each mutex is a global of type `mbedtls_threading_mutex_t`, initialised by `MUTEX_INIT` in `library/threading.c:182-190`." | WHY: The answer states that library/ spawns no threads and that library/threading.c provides the mutex abstraction (the globals and the lock function pointers) used by threaded callers.
